question: A researcher has produced separate findings for each of five regional markets and now wants them combined into one view. What should the combining request specify?
options: A) That the five regions should each appear in the combined view in order of the revenue they contribute to the business.
B) That the combined view should be shorter than the five sets of findings added together, to keep it readable.
C) How to handle findings that overlap and findings that conflict, so those decisions are made openly and not quietly.
D) That the strongest of the five sets of findings should be used as the template the other four are all rewritten into.
correct_answers: C) How to handle findings that overlap and findings that conflict, so those decisions are made openly and not quietly.
explanations: Revenue order affects presentation only, and it can bury a serious finding from a small market at the end of the document.
A length target shapes the summary but says nothing about which findings survive, so the reduction happens on unstated grounds.

Correct. Merging is where a genuine disagreement between regions can be smoothed into a single confident sentence. Saying in advance how overlaps and conflicts are treated keeps those differences visible, since a conflict between regions is often the most useful finding.
Forcing four regions into the shape of a fifth discards whatever each of them found that does not fit that template.
